analysis: The supplied units are test-only changes to .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py: a renamed cross-file-uncertainty test now expects no redundant local Opus rescan, and a new manual GitHub rerun test expects the review to hand off with no paid calls. The base tail (lines 1084-1404) and the head start (lines 1-565) are mostly unchanged context for the Bedrock lifecycle, repair, accounting-failure and fail-closed clearance tests. The provider-side canonical threat model (T-041 prefix cache, TB-002 and others) is not touched by this CI review tooling. No production provider, coordinator, key, attestation or cache code is modified, so there is no regression against the A-/TB-/T- entries. Clearance semantics asserted in the tests stay conservative: clean() is false on uncertainty, call limits, failed checkpoints or accounting errors, and a rerun yields manual review. Coverage limits: the production behavior (budget_runner, threat-model-review.py, the MANUAL_SCAN_RERUN_DISABLED implementation and the changed 949-982 hunk) is not visible beyond the truncated patch, and the head text stops at line 565. So the claim that production matches these tests is unverified, and the implementing change would need its own review. This is a limit on coverage rather than a finding.
